data.one_liner: A debug overlay providing log viewers, HTTP inspectors, and custom actions inside your app.
data.what_it_does: It implements a global debug overlay directly in your Flutter app, enabling on-device inspection of logs and HTTP requests. It supports custom widgets for global actions and offers default triggers like touch gestures or keyboard shortcuts.
use_when: You need to inspect logs and HTTP traffic directly on physical devices away from a computer.
You want a global overlay for custom debugging actions anywhere in your app.
avoid_when: You only need desktop-attached debugging tools like DevTools.
You want to avoid adding extra runtime overhead or third-party buckets for logging.
strengths: Global overlay works above app navigation.
Built-in integrations for popular HTTP clients like Dio and http.
Customizable trigger options for mobile and desktop.
weaknesses: Requires manual setup and wiring of LogBuckets and HttpBuckets.
May clutter production builds if not conditionally disabled.
data.setup_notes: Insert the DebugOverlay widget into the builder of your WidgetsApp or MaterialApp.

alternatives.name: talker
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides extensive logging, error handling, and a flexible UI package for debugging Flutter apps.
